 ∠BDC = 73°

questions.question: A boat goes 10 km upstream in 50 minutes, and the speed of the stream is 3 kmph. Find the speed of the boat in still water (in kmph).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Upstream Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Upstream Speed = 10 ÷ (50/60) = 10 × (6/5) = 12 kmph

Speed of boat in still water = Upstream Speed + Speed of stream

Speed of boat = 12 + 3 = 15 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 15 kmph.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance traveled upstream = 10 km

Time taken = 50 minutes

Speed of the stream = 3 kmph

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/371936b9be9e51e479f85e1fbe7246cf4cc86ef390d26e611fe737783a5d2ece.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water − Speed of stream

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken = 50 ÷ 60 hours = 5/6 hours

⇒ Upstream Speed = 10 ÷ (5/6)

⇒ Upstream Speed = 10 × (6/5) = 12 kmph

⇒ Let the speed of the boat in still water be u kmph.

⇒ 12 = u − 3

⇒ u = 12 + 3 = 15 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 15 kmph.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

When the boat moves in the direction of the stream. Downstream Speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream.

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If both upstream and downstream speeds are known: Speed of Boat = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

If both upstream and downstream speeds are known: Speed of Stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

questions.question: A vendor earns 10% on an investment but loses 10% on another investment. What will be the combined loss or gain if the two investments are in the ratio 1 ∶ 3?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A vendor earns 10% on one investment but loses 10% on another investment.

The two investments are in the ratio 1 ∶ 3

**Calculation:**

Let one investment be 100 then the other one is 300.

Total 300 +100 = 400 

Profit earn in 1st investment 100 × 10/100 = 10

Loss earn in 2nd investment 300 × 10/100 = 30

Total loss 30-10 = 20

Loss percentage will be 20/400 × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct option is 4**

questions.question: If sin (p + q) = 1 and cos (p - q) = (sqrt3)/(2), find p
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 sin (p + q) = 1

cos (p - q) = (sqrt3)/(2)

**Concept used:**

Sin90°= 1, cos**3**0° =(sqrt3)/(2) ** **

**Calculation:**

 sin (p + q) = 1

⇒ sin (p + q) = sin 90° 

⇒ p+q = 90°

Again,

cos (p - q) = (sqrt3)/(2)

⇒ cos (p - q) = cos 30° 

⇒ (p - q) = 30° 

p = 1/2 (p+q + p - q)

⇒ 1/2 (90+30) = 60°

questions.question: A person, who spends 68% of his monthly income, is able to save Rs. 14,720 per month. Find his total expenses.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expenditure = 68% of his monthly income.

Savings = Rs. 14,720 

**Concept used:**

Income = savings + expenditure

**Calculation:**

His total income is 100%

He spends 68%

So he saves 100 - 68 = 32%

So the value of 32 % = 14720

So the value of 68% = (14720 / 32)× 68 

⇒ Rs 31,280

**∴ The correct option is 3**

⇒ p² − q² = (27/4) − (3/4) = 24/4 = 6

⇒ 16pq = 16 × (3√3/2) × (√3/2) = 16 × 9/4 = 36

⇒ √16pq = √36 = 6
